Game Loop Lab

One jump, three screens. Each dot is one frame the player sees. Change the screen rate and the loop, then watch the jump height, the floor and the frames that do not move.

Sky Hopper, level 3. Goal: the same jump on every screen, reaching the 1.55 m ledge, never falling through the floor, and no frozen frames.

Lesson 011: fixed vs variable timestep

    
    
  
    

  
    
    
    What this shows
    
    
    
      
    Step size changes the answer
    Physics in steps is an estimate. Peak = 1.667 − 5 × step. A variable step gives every screen a different game. A fixed step gives every screen the same game.
    
      
    Big steps skip things
    A collision check only sees where the player is after a step. One 0.25 s step moves 3.125 m and jumps over a 0.5 m floor. Small fixed steps can't.
    
      
    Fixed needs two guards
    Interpolation hides the frames with no new step, for up to one step of delay. A step cap stops the spiral of death, but the real fix is a step that costs far less than 16.67 ms.
    
    
    
    
    This lab is a simulation, not a measurement. It uses the lesson's numbers: jump speed 10 m/s, gravity 30 m/s², semi-implicit Euler, a 0.5 m floor with a simple "where am I after the step" check, 60 Hz fixed step, 6 ms of drawing per frame. Time is counted in exact 1/720 s ticks, so 30, 60 and 144 Hz line up perfectly. Real frames jitter by a fraction of a millisecond, so a real 60 Hz game sometimes runs 0 or 2 steps in a frame.
